title: LFP vs Lead-Acid: Why Lithium Iron Phosphate Wins for Backup Power
excerpt: Lead-acid batteries have powered inverters for decades. Here's why lithium iron phosphate (LFP) now delivers more usable energy, longer life and lower lifetime cost.
alt: 12V 100Ah lithium LFP battery with charging clamps
author: "ThOR" BESS Team
body:
For years the default choice for home inverters, UPS systems and small solar setups has been the lead-acid battery. It is familiar and cheap to buy — but over its working life it is rarely the cheapest option. Lithium iron phosphate (LFP, or LiFePO₄) batteries have changed that equation.

## 1. More usable energy from the same rating
A lead-acid battery should not be regularly discharged much below half of its capacity; deep discharges shorten its life sharply. An LFP battery can routinely use most of its rated capacity. In practice, a 100Ah LFP battery gives you noticeably more real backup time than a 100Ah lead-acid battery.

## 2. Thousands of cycles instead of hundreds
Cycle life is where LFP pulls far ahead. Our "ThOR" LFP range is rated for 3,000 to 4,000 charge cycles with a service life of up to 9 years — several times what a typical lead-acid inverter battery delivers before replacement.

> Fewer replacements mean lower lifetime cost, less downtime and less waste.

## 3. No water top-ups, no acid, no fumes
LFP batteries are sealed and maintenance-free. There is no distilled water to add, no terminal corrosion to clean and no acid fumes, so they can sit safely indoors in homes, clinics and offices.

## 4. Safer chemistry
Among lithium chemistries, LFP is known for its thermal stability. Combined with a battery management system (BMS) that protects against over-charge, over-discharge, short circuit and over-temperature, it is one of the safest ways to store energy at home or on site.

## 5. Lighter and faster to charge
For the same usable energy, LFP batteries are much lighter than lead-acid, which makes installation easier. They also accept charge faster — useful when the grid is only available for a few hours or when charging from solar.

## When does lead-acid still make sense?
If a battery is used only a few times a year and upfront price is the only concern, lead-acid can still work. For anything that cycles regularly — daily solar storage, frequent power cuts, field equipment — LFP is the better long-term investment.

!! Looking for a direct lead-acid replacement? The "ThOR" LFP 12V 100Ah and 12V 150Ah models are designed for home inverters and solar systems.

title: What Is a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) and How Does It Work?
excerpt: A BESS stores electricity when it is available and delivers it when it's needed. Here's a clear guide to the parts, the benefits and where it's used.
author: "ThOR" BESS Team
body:
A Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) stores electrical energy in batteries and releases it when it is needed. It sounds simple, but a well-designed BESS changes how homes, businesses and even entire grids use power.

## The main building blocks
- **Battery cells and modules** — in "ThOR" BESS we use lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells for safety and long life.
- **Battery management system (BMS)** — monitors every cell's voltage, current and temperature, balances them and protects the pack.
- **Power conversion system** — inverters and chargers convert between the battery's DC power and the AC power your equipment uses.
- **Energy management and controls** — decide when to charge, when to discharge and how to respond to the grid.
- **Thermal management and safety systems** — keep the batteries in their ideal temperature range.

## How it works, step by step
When electricity is cheap, abundant or generated by solar and wind, the BESS charges. When the grid fails, demand peaks or renewables drop off, it discharges — within milliseconds. A "ThOR" system can switch over in about 15 ms, fast enough to act as an uninterruptible power supply.

## Why it matters
- **Backup power** — zero blackouts and minimal downtime for critical equipment.
- **Renewable integration** — stores daytime solar for use at night and smooths out the intermittency of wind and solar.
- **Cost savings** — time-of-use optimisation and peak shaving lower electricity bills.
- **Grid stability** — frequency regulation, voltage support and even black-start capability.
- **Cleaner air** — less reliance on diesel generators and fossil fuels.

## From a single box to a micro-grid
BESS scales. The same technology powers a portable unit on wheels, a trailer-mounted system for a hospital, and containerised installations of several megawatt-hours supporting a micro-grid. What changes is capacity, power rating and the enclosure — the principles stay the same.

title: How to Size a Battery for Your Home Inverter or Solar System
excerpt: Too small and you run out of backup; too big and you overspend. A simple, step-by-step method to choose the right battery voltage and capacity.
alt: Aerial view of a solar panel farm
author: "ThOR" BESS Team
body:
Choosing a battery does not need to be complicated. With three numbers — your load, your backup time and your system voltage — you can get very close to the right size.

## Step 1: Add up your load
List the appliances you want to run during a power cut and add up their wattage. For example: 4 LED lights (40 W), 2 fans (150 W), a Wi-Fi router (15 W) and a TV (100 W) come to about 305 W.

## Step 2: Decide how long you need backup
Multiply the load by the hours of backup you want. 305 W × 4 hours = about 1,220 Wh (1.2 kWh) of energy.

## Step 3: Allow for losses
Inverters are not 100% efficient. Add roughly 15–20% headroom: 1,220 Wh × 1.2 ≈ 1,460 Wh.

## Step 4: Match your system voltage
Check your inverter's battery voltage — usually 12 V, 24 V or 48 V. Divide the energy by the voltage to get the capacity in amp-hours (Ah):
- 12 V system: 1,460 ÷ 12 ≈ 122 Ah → a 12V 150Ah battery
- 24 V system: 1,460 ÷ 24 ≈ 61 Ah → a 24V 100Ah battery

!! With LFP you can use most of the rated capacity. With lead-acid you would need roughly twice the Ah rating for the same backup.

## Step 5: Think about charging
If you are charging from solar, make sure your panels and charge controller can refill the battery during the day. For daily solar cycling, the long cycle life of LFP makes a big difference to lifetime cost.

## Quick guide
- **Small home, lights and fans:** 12V 100Ah–150Ah
- **Larger home or small office:** 12V 230Ah or 24V 100Ah–230Ah
- **Hybrid solar, clinics, retail:** 48V 100Ah
- **Whole-home backup, commercial:** 48V 280Ah / 300Ah

Not sure? Share your appliance list with our team and we'll recommend the right "ThOR" LFP battery.

title: Micro-grids: Powering Rural India with Solar, Wind and Storage
excerpt: Decentralised micro-grids combine local renewables with battery storage to bring stable, round-the-clock power to villages, islands and remote sites.
alt: "ThOR" BESS micro-grid powering a village with solar and wind
author: "ThOR" BESS Team
body:
A micro-grid is a local power network that can generate, store and distribute electricity on its own — or connect to the main grid when it is available. For rural, tribal and island communities, it can be the difference between a few hours of unreliable supply and power around the clock.

## The role of storage
Solar produces power only in the day and wind comes and goes. Battery storage is what turns these sources into a dependable supply: it captures surplus energy and releases it at night or when the wind drops.

## What a "ThOR" BESS micro-grid includes
- Solar, wind, bio-fuel or hydro generation — whatever is available locally
- Containerised "ThOR" BESS storage, typically 1 MWh to 5 MWh per model
- Smart controls that balance generation, storage and demand
- Optional connection to the main grid

> A micro-grid can run independently or link to the larger network — keeping power stable either way.

## Benefits for communities
- **Continuous supply** for homes, schools, health centres and small businesses
- **Livelihoods** — cold storage, irrigation pumps and workshops can run reliably
- **Lower costs** compared with running diesel generators
- **Cleaner air** and lower carbon emissions

## Beyond villages
The same approach works for industrial parks, campuses, defence installations and disaster-relief camps — anywhere that needs energy independence and resilience.

title: e-Generator vs Diesel Generator: The Practical Differences
excerpt: Noise, fumes, fuel logistics and maintenance — a side-by-side look at how a battery e-Generator compares with a conventional diesel genset.
author: "ThOR" BESS Team
body:
Diesel generators have long been the answer to power cuts and off-grid work. A battery-based e-Generator does the same job in a very different way — storing energy instead of burning fuel.

## Noise
A diesel genset is loud and usually has to be kept outside. The "ThOR" e-Generator runs silently (under 28 dB), so it can sit inside a clinic, office or tent.

## Emissions
Diesel engines release exhaust fumes and CO₂ wherever they run. An e-Generator produces zero emissions at the point of use, and when charged from solar or wind the whole cycle can be clean.

## Fuel and logistics
Diesel has to be bought, transported, stored and guarded. An e-Generator charges from the grid, solar, wind, a vehicle or other renewable sources.

## Switchover
A generator engine has to start before power returns. A "ThOR" e-Generator switches over in about 15 milliseconds — fast enough that sensitive equipment keeps running.

## Maintenance
Engines need oil changes, filters and regular servicing. An e-Generator has no engine, so maintenance is minimal. Standard units carry a 5-year warranty, with AMC options available.

## Portability
"ThOR" e-Generators are built in rugged carbon / glass-fibre composite enclosures and are up to three times lighter than comparable fossil-fuel units.

!! When is diesel still used? For very long runtimes far from any charging source, a hybrid set-up — e-Generator plus solar, with diesel only as a last resort — often gives the best of both.

## Customised to the job
Every e-Generator is built to order: light-duty portable units (2–15 kWh), vehicle-mounted medium-duty systems (20–150 kWh) and containerised heavy-duty systems up to 5 MWh.

title: Identifying Key User Groups for LFP Battery Applications
excerpt: Lithium iron phosphate batteries are revolutionising energy storage. Their safety and long cycle life make them ideal for many user groups.
author: "ThOR" BESS Team
body:
Lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries combine safety, long life and low maintenance. That makes them a strong fit for a wide range of users — from households to defence teams.

## Homes and small businesses
Frequent power cuts, rising bills and rooftop solar all point to LFP. It replaces lead-acid inverter batteries with longer backup and no maintenance.

## Healthcare
Clinics, hospitals and mobile medical camps need power that never drops. LFP storage with fast switchover keeps ventilators, CPAP machines, monitors and vaccine refrigerators running.

## Telecom and communication
Remote towers and communication equipment need reliable, compact storage that can handle daily cycling and heat.

## Agriculture
Solar-charged storage runs irrigation pumps, lighting and farm equipment without diesel — and powers agri-drones in the field.

## Defence and disaster response
Silent operation, a low heat signature and portability make LFP-based systems valuable for field command, radar, communication and relief camps.

## Mobility and EV charging
From e-bikes and robots to portable EV chargers and fleet charging stations, LFP's cycle life and safety are a natural match.

> The right chemistry matters — but so does the right size. Choosing the correct voltage and capacity is the next step.

title: Clean Power When It Matters Most: Energy Storage for Disaster Response
excerpt: When floods, cyclones or earthquakes cut the grid, portable battery storage keeps rescue teams, shelters and medical camps running.
alt: "ThOR" BESS providing emergency power in a flood zone
author: "ThOR" BESS Team
body:
In a disaster, the grid is often the first thing to fail — and power is one of the first things responders need. Lighting, communication, medical devices and water pumps all depend on it.

## Why battery storage fits emergencies
- **Rapid deployment** — portable and vehicle-mounted units can be moved in quickly.
- **Fuel independence** — no need to transport diesel into affected areas; units can recharge from solar.
- **Silent and clean** — safe to run inside shelters and medical tents.
- **Reliable for life-saving equipment** — fast switchover keeps sensitive devices running.

## Where it helps
- Rescue operations and command centres
- Relief shelters and community kitchens
- Field hospitals and first-responder medical kits
- Communication, GPS and satellite equipment
- Emergency lighting and water purification

!! "ThOR" e-Generators are designed for first responders, defence and disaster teams — from light-duty portable units to truck-mounted megawatt-scale systems.

## Planning ahead
The best time to plan emergency power is before it's needed. Pre-positioned storage, charged and ready, lets teams restore essential services within minutes of arrival.

body:
